presentation.title: Check Washing and Altered Payee
presentation.summary: Practice comparing a processed check with your records, reporting an altered check promptly, reviewing other exposed checks, and preserving evidence privately.
presentation.practiceGoal: Use a trusted bank channel to inspect an unexpected check, report the full mismatch, and follow the bank's guidance without assuming reimbursement is guaranteed.

warningSigns.sign: A processed check has an amount or payee that does not match your records.
A mailed payment never reaches the intended company.
Nearby check numbers are missing, duplicated, or used unexpectedly.
A second altered check appears after the first mismatch.
An unexpected alert link asks you to sign in instead of using your known bank channel.

finalReview.safestAction: Open the bank app or statement you already trust, compare the processed check with your records, and report every mismatch promptly.

realWorldActions.action: Tell the bank the original payee, original amount, check number, mailing date, and every other outstanding check you know about.
Ask the bank about monitoring, stop payments, and whether the exposed account number should be replaced.
Review nearby check numbers, missing mail, recurring payments, deposits, and automatic withdrawals.
Preserve check images, transaction details, alerts, notes, and bank case information privately.
Use secure mail collection and review account activity regularly. Follow the bank's instructions because procedures and recovery options vary.

artifact.senderStatus: Simulated alert; verify in the known bank app
artifact.heading: Check 214 paid for $4,860
artifact.message: A check was paid to an unfamiliar person. An email copy of the alert also includes a Review Transaction button.
artifact.transcript: A simulated bank alert says, "Check 214 paid for $4,860," to a person the learner does not recognize. An email copy includes a Review Transaction button. The learner does not remember writing a check for that amount or to that payee.

warningSigns.sign: The amount is much larger than expected.
The payee is unfamiliar.

choice.title: Use the button in the alert email
choice.subtitle: Follow the email's Review Transaction route.

artifact.heading: Compare your record with the processed check
artifact.message: Your register says check 214 was written for $86 to Green Valley Utilities. The processed image shows $4,860 to an unfamiliar payee. The check number and signature look familiar.

requestedInformation.item: Your record: $86 to Green Valley Utilities
Processed image: $4,860 to an unfamiliar payee

The processed check image shows the same check number and a familiar-looking signature, but the amount is $4,860 and the payee is unfamiliar. Green Valley Utilities and Riverbend Bank are fictional.

warningSigns.sign: The processed amount does not match the register.

feedback.explanation: Scammers and thieves create these situations. Preserving evidence is a practical step, not a reason for shame. The terminal outcome will acknowledge the additional exposure even when recovery is now handled well.

warningSigns.sign: The altered checks may be connected to other account activity.

artifact.heading: Late recovery covers the full check sequence
artifact.message: Additional check exposure occurred, but the learner now gives the bank a complete report and preserves the evidence privately.
artifact.transcript: A second altered check or delayed report remains part of the case. The learner now works with the real bank on stop payments, monitoring, account security, legitimate payment transitions, and private evidence preservation. Recovery is not guaranteed, but further harm may be reduced.

outcome.label: Additional exposure; strong recovery
outcome.heading: You responded fully after the delay
outcome.explanation: The late safe action improves containment, while the outcome still acknowledges that more check activity occurred.

warningSigns.sign: A later safe choice cannot erase the second check or earlier exposure.

artifact.heading: The additional check incident is only partly documented
artifact.message: Some records or protections are in place, but the broader sequence and account exposure remain incompletely addressed.
artifact.transcript: The learner delayed reporting and then preserved only part of the evidence or recovery plan. The real bank may still need the complete check sequence, mail history, and access details. Additional loss has already occurred or remains under review.

outcome.label: Additional exposure; recovery incomplete
outcome.heading: Important parts of the incident remain unresolved
outcome.explanation: Partial action is useful, but the second check and delayed containment require a broader bank-guided response.

warningSigns.sign: The earlier delay and incomplete recovery leave account risk open.

artifact.heading: Additional loss and missing evidence remain unresolved
artifact.message: The delayed report allowed more check exposure, and deleting records or avoiding the bank makes recovery harder.
artifact.transcript: More than one check may have been altered, and the learner has not preserved the full record or completed a bank-guided security review. The learner can still contact the real bank, explain the complete timeline, and seek trusted support without blame.

outcome.label: Additional loss; risk ongoing
outcome.heading: The earlier consequences remain active
outcome.explanation: It is still possible to stop, preserve what remains, and move recovery to the real bank.

warningSigns.sign: The first mismatch was followed by additional exposure and incomplete recovery.

artifact.heading: The bank has a complete report
artifact.message: You documented the altered checks, reviewed the broader exposure, and preserved evidence privately.
artifact.transcript: The learner reports the mismatch, reviews related checks and mail exposure, follows the fictional bank's security guidance, and preserves a private evidence record. The bank will determine available options; the scenario does not promise reimbursement.

outcome.label: Complete bank-centered response
outcome.heading: You responded to the full pattern
outcome.explanation: Prompt reporting, broader account review, secure payment habits, and private evidence give the bank the clearest information without guaranteeing a particular recovery result.

artifact.heading: The recovery record is incomplete
artifact.message: The paper register helps, but processed images, alerts, or related-check details are missing.
artifact.transcript: The learner keeps part of the incident record but not the complete evidence. The bank may still help, and the learner can ask what records remain available in the account history. Future review should include the full check sequence and account exposure.

outcome.label: Partial recovery record
outcome.heading: Some useful information was preserved
outcome.explanation: The response reduced part of the risk, but missing evidence or incomplete review can make follow-up harder.

artifact.heading: Evidence and account risks remain
artifact.message: Deleting the records does not erase the altered checks or protect the exposed account.
artifact.transcript: The learner deletes useful records while altered checks and possible account exposure remain. This is not a personal failure. Contact the real bank through a trusted channel, explain the event fully, ask what records the bank retains, and follow its security guidance.

outcome.label: Recovery delayed
outcome.heading: The bank still needs the full story
outcome.explanation: Acting now can still help document the fraud and secure the account, but recovery is not guaranteed.
